attendees.role: town manager / presenter of warrant articles

budget_items.what_was_said: Outside CPA firm Eric Kincherf CPA will complete the entire FY25 closeout; free cash likely will not be certified by special town meeting, but no free-cash appropriations are planned so there should be no impact.

Governor Healey's reported pullback of local earmarks did not affect Lunenburg's two earmarks, which have now flowed to the state agencies; the town requested the funds quickly in case they are pulled back.

budget_items.topic: Article 2 - FY26 budget amendment, salary reserve transfers
budget_items.what_was_said: Transfers from salary reserve are planned for the police chief, the new finance director, and police wages from collective bargaining.

budget_items.topic: Article 2 - new growth actual vs. estimate
budget_items.what_was_said: New growth actuals are coming in well above the budgeted estimate, prompting a raise-and-appropriate; members disputed the exact figure.
Additional unanticipated funds may be needed in the library to cover a series of maternity leaves; amount not yet estimated.
A bill from Heywood Hospital for employee health needs a 9/10 vote at special town meeting; recommended deferral to town meeting.
Additional funds are needed for stormwater/MS4 consulting after switching consultants, to be transferred from unexpended prior-year capital (ADA Ritter project).
A pass-through of retained earnings to the general fund and back for PAC-related expenses is being cleaned up into a direct transfer from retained earnings to the enterprise fund.
An additional new amount is being added for PAC's videographer staffing on top of the retained-earnings transfer.
PAC's fee revenue is running well below its budget/retained-earnings draw, raising concern about sustaining operations on declining cable receipts.
Funds from the cemetery sale-of-lots account will be transferred to the capital article fund to straighten and repair headstones.
A standalone fund is proposed to hire professional project estimators for capital projects, after several in-house estimates came in far under actual bids.

budget_items.topic: Article 8 - special education reserve fund cap
budget_items.what_was_said: The proposed reserve fund cannot exceed a stated share of annual net school spending; article establishes but does not fund the reserve.

budget_items.topic: Article 9 - 41A deferral interest rate and income threshold
budget_items.what_was_said: A prior town meeting lowered the deferral interest rate; this article proposes raising the income eligibility threshold to match 100% of the state circuit-breaker amount.
Printing and mailing the full warrant booklet to all households costs an estimated amount annually, cited as a reason to switch to a postcard notice.

budget_items.topic: Article 16 - SAP vacation system transition cost
budget_items.what_was_said: Changing employees over to a new vacation accrual system under the redrafted personnel bylaw will carry a cost that has not yet been quantified pending the attorney's final draft.

New growth for FY26, originally projected at $400,000, appears to be coming in around $1.3 million, driven by corrected assessed values and personal property findings; not yet confirmed with the assessor.

decisions.decision: Finance committee will defer its vote on Article 2 (FY26 budget amendment) all the way to town meeting.
Finance committee will defer its vote on Article 3 (prior-year bill) all the way to town meeting.
Committee agreed to raise PAC's operating-budget sustainability as a topic at the next tri-board meeting rather than during PAC's own budget presentation.
The tri-board will give the school budget its own dedicated meeting night rather than combining it with other topics.
Chair will poll members on availability for a tri-board meeting during Thanksgiving week since November 18th (town meeting night) will not work.
Debate on Article 17 (eliminating the personnel committee) and its financial impact will be taken up at the November 13th public hearing/recommendation meeting.

minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Finance Committee walked through all 17 articles of the special town meeting warrant (FY26 budget amendments, transfers, a special education reserve fund, a 41A tax deferral expansion, MBTA zoning compliance, and several SAP/personnel bylaw changes), asking questions but deliberately deferring any recommendations until the November 13th public hearing. The only formal votes taken were procedural: approving three sets of prior tri-board minutes and adjournment.

what_happened.line: Finance Committee reviewed all 17 special town meeting warrant articles but deferred recommendations to the Nov. 13 public hearing.
Two articles on the FY26 budget amendment and a prior-year hospital bill will go to town meeting without a committee recommendation.
New growth actuals are coming in above the budgeted estimate, prompting a raise-and-appropriate article; members disputed the exact figure.
PAC's fee revenue is running below its budget and retained-earnings draw, raising a sustainability question the tri-board will take up separately.
The tri-board will give the school budget its own dedicated meeting, likely during Thanksgiving week since Nov. 18 town meeting night will not work.

why_it_matters: Town meeting voters will decide the FY26 budget amendment, a prior-year bill, a special education reserve fund, and other transfers without a Finance Committee recommendation attached until Nov. 13.
A proposed 41A expansion and MBTA zoning compliance article are both on the warrant and could affect senior tax deferrals and local zoning rules.
PAC's budget shortfall and the personnel committee's proposed elimination are unresolved questions that residents may hear more about at the Nov. 13 hearing or a later tri-board meeting.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records describe the same warrant articles and dollar figures largely consistently where both give a number, but the official minutes are a narrative summary that omits nearly all the granular figures our transcript-based minutes captured, while the official minutes contain a whole section (staff transitions, CPA contract, tax classification hearing) and several members' questions that our minutes never mention at all. The one thing a reader should check first is who is actually responsible for polling members on tri-board availability (the Chair per ours vs. the Town Manager per the official minutes) and whether Article 2/3 votes are really deferred all the way to town meeting or to the November 13 public hearing as the official minutes' announcement implies.
